notes: §1985:VII.4.3.4 GR20 states four rules for a set of files that resides on a multiple file reel: a, "Not more than one of the files may be in the open mode at one time."; b, "There is no constraint on the order in which files may be opened in the input mode."; c, an OPEN OUTPUT needs every file of a lower position number to "already exist on the reel at the time the OPEN statement is executed" and none of a higher one; d, "Each of the files must be a sequential file." Rule d is decidable from the source text and is enforced: ScreenMultipleFileClause records each MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause's files on FileModel.MultipleFileReels (the clause is accepted at 85 by VisitMultipleFileClause, COBOL0902 from 2002), and CheckOpenModeForFile, called by BindOpen for every file-name of every OPEN, reports COBOL6816 when a file of the set is not sequential. Rules a and c restrict the program on a reel device and state no action of the processor (no I-O status and no unsuccessful OPEN is defined for them); the reel is hardware the implementation does not claim (§1985:C.3, item 7: "The MULTIPLE FILE TAPE clause is dependent upon a reel type of device."; §1985:I.1.5.2.5.1: "Language elements that pertain to specific hardware components for which support is not claimed need not be implemented."), and docs/CONFORMANCE.md section 3.4 records them as a null facility: no file is placed on a reel, so no order of opening or position constrains a host file. Rule b asks for no constraint and none exists. Probed at --std 85: a clause naming a relative file draws COBOL6816 at each OPEN of a file of the set (INPUT and OUTPUT) and none at an OPEN of a file outside it; three sequential files at POSITION 1, 3 and 5 are created in order and opened INPUT in the order 5, 1, 3 with status 00; two files of one clause open at the same time both answer 00. The witness creates the files at positions 1 and 2 in order and reads the second. Not covered by this verdict: the witness assigns both files to one implementor-name, which is one host file with or without the clause, so its second OPEN OUTPUT replaces the first file's record (probed: FILE-A then reads FILEB-DATA); POSITION does not separate files, the unprovided reel function.

next.reason: 1985: "Whenever a set of files resides on a multiple file reel, and one of this set of files is referenced in an OPEN statement"; 2023: "No multiple file reel rule in OPEN GRs 14.9.27.4-1..26 or any candidate; position numbers are not addressed anywhere". 2023 OPEN rules and the file clauses shown lack multiple file reels and position numbers; the MULTIPLE FILE feature these rules govern is absent from 2023.
